children: rose 0.53% to $193.12 at 8:15 a.m. ET in October 20 premarket trading after raising its full-year outlook. Reuters reported an earnings beat and a record backlog. But the headline profit jump needs a closer look: a cost-recovery benefit supplied a hefty slice of the increase.

RTX's quarterly release put adjusted earnings at $2.26 a share, up from $1.70 a year earlier, including $0.25 from IEEPA cost recovery. Strip out that benefit and the figure comes to $2.01, still roughly 18.2% above last year. That is a comparison calculation, rather than a company-reported adjusted measure, and other unusual items may remain. Sales reached $24.965 billion, backlog hit $340 billion, and management lifted its annual adjusted earnings forecast to $7.65$7.75 a share from $7.10$7.25. GAAP earnings were $1.89 a share.

The GF Score of 85 out of 100 shows growth as RTX's strongest category, while the weaker GF Value reading suggests valuation deserves closer scrutiny. The earnings math reinforces that distinction. Cost recovery contributed roughly 45% of the 56-cent increase in adjusted earnings, so investors should avoid carrying the entire jump into future forecasts. The backlog provides revenue visibility. Turning those orders into sustained profit growth is the next test.

title: RTX Stocks Rise as Earnings Gain Includes a 25-Cent Recovery
